# Dockerfile for amg2023
# Target: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, recent environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, Git, certificates, and OpenMPI
# - build-essential, gfortran, make: For compiling the C/Fortran application
# - git: To clone the source code repository
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications (e.g., git clone)
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: The MPI implementation and development headers
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes
# These settings ensure robust performance by forcing TCP communication over container networks
# and preventing common issues with process binding and shared memory.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_hwloc_base_binding_policy=none

# Create a temporary directory for the build process
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the latest branch of the amg2023 source code, build it,
# install the executable to a system PATH, and clean up the source code.
# This entire process is in a single RUN layer to optimize image size.
RUN git clone https://github.com/llnl/amg.git && \
    # FIX: Build from the project root directory to ensure all library
    # dependencies are compiled before the final executable.
    cd amg && \
    make && \
    # The executable is created in the 'test' subdirectory after a successful build.
    # Copy the executable to a system location on the PATH.
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    # Clean up the build directory to keep the final image clean
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /

# Default command to run the application's help message,
# which also serves as a quick verification that the build was successful
# and the executable is in the PATH.
CMD ["amg", "--help"]

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the AMG2023 benchmark
# on a single AWS CPU-based Kubernetes node using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: amg2023-problem2-test
  # The job will be deployed to the 'default' namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods to deploy for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to ensure the entire job runs on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The number of MPI tasks to run.
  # This corresponds to the -n flag for `flux run`.
  tasks: 4

  # Keep pods and services running after the job completes for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Fail on any error and print it to the logs.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # This is the command that `flux run` will execute.
      # Runs AMG with problem type 2 and a small problem size (4x4x4 grid).
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
      
      # This is not the main launcher pod where the user interface is.
      launcher: false
